join_order.notes: Driver: single it_id selects pi slice; pi.note IS NOT NULL filter applied inline.
Per pid, scan aka slice; pass if any aka has len>0 AND (memchr(name,'a') || name[0]=='A').
Per pid expand to ci rows; read ci_movie[ci_row] to get t_id.
1980<=y<=2010 && y!=INT32_MIN; direct array indexing by t_id.
Per t_id, enumerate ml rows; verify ml_link_type_id in target_lt_ids.
Tiny target_lt_ids set (≤4 ids out of 18); use std::array<bool,19> bitset for O(1) membership.

filters.predicate: len>0 AND (name LIKE '%a%' OR name LIKE 'A%')

data_structures.gender_codes: int8_t code_m, code_f resolved from name/gender.dict at runtime
data_structures.title_year: mmap int32 array, direct indexed by t_id-1
data_structures.aggregation: per-thread (min_name_off,min_name_len) and (min_pi_info_off,min_pi_info_len); merge with lexicographic compare against name.dat / person_info.info.dat

parallelism.notes: Partition the pi slice [lo,hi) for target_it_id into morsels (e.g., 4096 rows each). Each thread maintains local MIN(name) and MIN(pi.info); final reduction lex-compares via the .dat buffers.

notes: Per pi row in target_it_id slice: (1) check note non-empty; (2) pid=pi_person[pi_row]; (3) read name_pcode_cf[pid-1]: lex 'A'<=s<='F' (treat as bytewise; empty fails); (4) gender check with optional A%-name condition; (5) aka semi-join via offsets; (6) expand ci; (7) per t_id year filter; (8) ml semi-join with target_lt_ids; (9) if any match → update MIN(name) for pid and MIN(pi.info) for pi_row.

Short-circuit: once a pid passes aka semi-join and name MIN candidate is updated, MIN(pi.info) still requires at least one full match through ml; track them independently — name min is conditional on the full join succeeding, so update both only after a match is found.

BETWEEN 'A' AND 'F' on name_pcode_cf: inclusive, so accept strings s with s>='A' and s<='F\xff...' — using std::string_view lex compare with 'A' lower bound and 'G' exclusive upper is incorrect; use s>="A" && s<="F" semantics: a string 'F' is accepted, 'Fa' is rejected (since 'Fa'>'F' lex). Implementation: compare to literal 'A' lower and to 'F' upper using strncmp-style bytewise compare.
